To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) firms with exchange-traded options are associated with five firm-specific attributes: (1a) larger firm size (2) higher analyst coverage (3) higher institutional ownership (4) higher share trading volume, and(5) more frequent Wall Street Journal Index releases, (2) the price-earn-ings relation of firms with exchange-trade options is stronger than that of non-option firms, and (3) option firms exhibit less post-FYE drift in stock prices than non-option
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of option trading on the price-earnngs relation.
the relation between option trading and the price-earn- ings relation.
the effect of option listing on the priceearnings (P/E) relation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the option market has a positive impact on the timeliness and availability of information about firms.
the option trading and the relation between price and earnings are not necessarily the same.
the price-earns relation of option firms and nonoption firms is not significantly different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the option markets have been a significant source of new information and that the option markets are a significant source of price discovery.
we have shown that option firms have a different predisclosure information structure than nonoption firms.
option trading affects predisclosure information environments and, consequently, the price-earnin gs relation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the option market is a very important source of information for the stock market.
there is a strong relationship between the number of options traded and the number of analysts covering the stock.
the price- earnings ratio is a useful measure of the quality of earnings.
